members: Aripiprazole: D2/5-HT1A partial agonist, 5-HT2A antagonist; Original Pip (StahlNeuro p.228)
Brexpiprazole: SDAM, lower D2 intrinsic activity, strong 5-HT1A partial / Alpha-1B/1D antagonist; Second Pip (StahlNeuro p.229, p.239)
Cariprazine: D3 > D2 selective partial agonist, active metabolite DDCAR T1/2 = 1-3 weeks; The Rip (StahlNeuro p.230, p.240)
drug_class.mechanism: D2 dopamine system stabilizer (partial agonism / Goldilocks mechanism); D2 receptor occupancy required = 80%-85% (StahlNeuro p.43, p.189-191, p.348; Dulcan p.795)
kinetics: Aripiprazole T1/2 = 75h (Dehydro-aripiprazole 94h), CYP2D6/3A4 (StahlKids p.42; Dulcan p.787)
Brexpiprazole T1/2 = 91h, CYP2D6/3A4 (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.239)
Cariprazine T1/2 = 2-5d (DDCAR 1-3 weeks), CYP3A4/2D6 (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.239)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: 1-2 weeks for acute symptoms; 2-4 weeks for steady state (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.41)

items: Aripiprazole FDA approved: Schizophrenia (ages 13-17) (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.37), Bipolar I Mania/Mixed (ages 10-17) (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.37), Autism Irritability (ages 6-17) (Dulcan p.150, p.787; StahlKids p.37), Tourette's Disorder (ages 6-18) (Dulcan p.447, p.787; StahlKids p.37), MDD adjunct in adults (StahlKids p.37)
Brexpiprazole FDA approved: Adult Schizophrenia, MDD adjunct in adults; no pediatric approval (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.239)

Cariprazine FDA approved: Adult Schizophrenia (superior in negative symptoms), Bipolar I Mania/Mixed, Bipolar Depression (1.5-3 mg/day); no pediatric approval (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.240, p.342-344)
Akathisia: most prominent class side effect; 5%-12% in youth on Aripiprazole (Dulcan p.823; StahlKids p.41). Brexpiprazole has lower akathisia (StahlNeuro p.239)

Prolactin-sparing / reducing: D2 partial agonism in pituitary lactotrophs suppresses prolactin; low-dose Aripiprazole (1.5-5 mg/day) reverses Risperidone hyperprolactinemia (StahlNeuro p.192; StahlKids p.49; Dulcan p.820, p.825)
Weight / Metabolic: low risk in adults (StahlNeuro p.198); moderate in youth (13%-33% with >=7% weight gain) (Dulcan p.810, p.820)
Tardive Dyskinesia: ~0.4%/year in pediatric populations due to lack of D2 up-regulation (Dulcan p.823; StahlNeuro p.177)
NMS: rare, CPK > 1000 U/L, hyperthermia, rigidity (DSM p.811; Dulcan p.823-824)
key_numbers: Pediatric >=7% weight gain rate = 13%-33% (Dulcan p.810, p.820)
Tardive Dyskinesia annual incidence = 0.4% in youth (Dulcan p.823)

items: BMI & Weight: baseline, monthly for first 3 months, then quarterly (Dulcan p.820; StahlKids p.37)
Fasting Glucose & Lipids: baseline, 3 months, then annually (Dulcan p.820)
AIMS / BARS (EPS/Akathisia): baseline and every 6 months (Dulcan p.820, p.823)
Prolactin: symptom-driven only, routine monitoring not recommended (Dulcan p.820; StahlKids p.37)
key_numbers: BMI check interval = monthly for 3 months, then every 3 months (Dulcan p.820)
Fasting Glucose & Lipids = baseline, 3 months, then annual (Dulcan p.820)
BMI Z-score increase threshold = >=0.5 requires action (Dulcan p.820)

items: Aripiprazole pediatric dosing: Schizophrenia/Bipolar 10-30 mg/day; ASD 5-15 mg/day; Tourette's 5-20 mg/day. Start at 2 mg/day with slow titration to avoid nausea/activation (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.41)
Brexpiprazole adult dosing: Schizophrenia 2-4 mg/day; MDD adjunct 2 mg/day (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.239)
Cariprazine adult dosing: Schizophrenia/Mania 1.5-6.0 mg/day; Bipolar Depression 1.5-3.0 mg/day (Dulcan p.787; StahlNeuro p.239-240, p.342)
Pediatric pharmacokinetics: increased CYP2D6/3A4 clearance in pre-pubertal children leads to shorter half-life (35-55h for Aripiprazole vs 75h in adults) (StahlKids p.38, p.42)
Cross-titration protocol: 2-4 weeks overlap required when switching from D2 full antagonist to prevent rebound psychosis (StahlKids p.43; Dulcan p.796; StahlNeuro p.238)
key_numbers: Aripiprazole pediatric starting dose = 2 mg/day (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.41)
Cariprazine Bipolar Depression dose = 1.5-3.0 mg/day (StahlNeuro p.342)
Cross-titration duration = 2-4 weeks (StahlKids p.43; Dulcan p.796)

high_yield: D2 partial agonism acts as Net Antagonist in hyper-dopaminergic states and Net Agonist in hypo-dopaminergic states (Goldilocks / Stabilizer) (StahlNeuro p.43, p.189-191)
Requires 80%-85% D2 occupancy for antipsychotic efficacy compared to 60%-70% for full antagonists (StahlNeuro p.348; Dulcan p.795)
Cariprazine has extreme D3 > D2 selectivity (1000x higher affinity than dopamine), proving superior in negative symptoms and bipolar depression (StahlNeuro p.230, p.240, p.343-345)
Aripiprazole is the ONLY partial agonist with FDA pediatric approvals (EOS 13+, Bipolar 10+, ASD 6+, Tourette's 6+) (Dulcan p.787; StahlKids p.37)
Partial agonists do NOT elevate prolactin and lower baseline prolactin; low-dose Aripiprazole reverses Risperidone-induced hyperprolactinemia (StahlNeuro p.192; Dulcan p.820, p.825)

Abrupt switch from D2 full antagonist to partial agonist triggers severe rebound psychosis due to up-regulated supersensitive D2 receptors, requiring a 2-4 week cross-titration (StahlKids p.43; Dulcan p.796; StahlNeuro p.238)
